about: Validator audit corpus. Each case holds durable evidence, a diff, and claims whose truth is known. Planted claims are false in a labeled way; the validator must drop them or move them to hypotheses. Supported claims must stay. Run: git story study audit study/validator-audit/corpus.json

events.fact: goal: stop duplicate job execution under retries
events.excerpt: Jobs run twice when the worker retries after a timeout. Make execution exactly-once.
The lease expires while a slow job still runs, so a retry grabs the lock and runs the job again. Dropping the Redis lock.
Use optimistic row versioning on the jobs table: a retry that sees a newer version skips the job. No new infrastructure, and CI has no Redis.

diff.diff:
@@ -10,7 +10,12 @@ def run(job):
-    with redis_lock(job.id, lease=30):
-        execute(job)
+    row = jobs.get(job.id)
+    if row.version != job.version:
+        return  # a newer attempt owns this job
+    if jobs.bump_version(job.id, expected=row.version):
+        execute(job)

@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+ALTER TABLE jobs ADD COLUMN version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

claims.claim: Replaced the Redis lock with optimistic row versioning on the jobs table
Row versioning was chosen because it needs no new infrastructure and CI has no Redis
A Redis lock with a 30s lease was dropped because the lease could expire while a slow job still ran
The retry lock suite passed 50 of 50 runs
Row versioning was chosen because it is faster than Redis under load
A Redis lock with a 60s lease was dropped because the lease could expire
The retry lock suite passed 50 of 50 runs with the Redis lock
Added exponential backoff between job retries
Kept the Redis lock as a fallback when the version check fails

events.fact: goal: move password hashing off bcrypt
events.excerpt: Security review flagged bcrypt's 72-byte input limit. Move to argon2id.
Passphrases longer than 72 bytes are silently truncated by bcrypt. Use argon2id with memory cost 64 MiB, 3 iterations.
Existing bcrypt hashes must keep working. Rehash on next successful login.

claims.claim: New passwords are hashed with argon2id at 64 MiB memory and 3 iterations
bcrypt was replaced because it silently truncates passphrases longer than 72 bytes
Existing bcrypt hashes are rehashed with argon2id on the next successful login
argon2id was chosen because it won the Password Hashing Competition
New passwords are hashed with argon2id at 64 MiB memory and 4 iterations
All existing bcrypt hashes are migrated to argon2id in a one-off batch job
The agent decided to rehash on login to avoid a forced password reset

events.fact: goal: fix invoice dates off by one day
events.excerpt: Invoices for customers in UTC-5 show the previous day.
Invoice dates are calendar dates. Parsing them as UTC midnight shifts them for negative offsets. Store and send them as plain YYYY-MM-DD strings.

Calendar dates parsed as UTC midnight shifted to the previous day for customers with negative UTC offsets
Invoice dates are now stored in the customer's local time zone
The database column was changed from TIMESTAMP to DATE
The invoice suite passed 64 of 64 tests, including new tests for UTC-5
